newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nelson the stud parrot awarded A$12,300 damages.
newsitem.headline: Nelson the stud parrot awarded A$12,300 damages.

text.p: The owner of an exotic parrot was awarded A$12,300 (US$9,700) in damages on Friday after a court ruled a veterinarian endangered the bird's "possible stud career" by breaking its leg during treatment.
New South Wales district court judge Terrence Christie determined that the payment should include A$2,500 for "stress and inconvenience" to Nelson the macaw's owner, Roger Schlup.
Schlup, who began the action last month, accused bird speclialist Ross Perry of negligently breaking Nelson's leg while treating the rare blue and gold South American male bird two years ago.
"Nelson is very weak on his leg," Schlup told reporters outside the court. "That is the heart-breaking part, having to see a bird suffer."
Schlup had told the court Nelson was left with a significant deformity of the left leg which affected its ability to mate.
Macaws are monogamous and must engage in a complex and strenuous mating ritual because of a lack of external genitalia, the court heard.
Schlup told the court in a statement the male and female birds stand next to each other on a perch and twist around to "align their rear ends".
Once in position, the pair of birds then use "considerable force" to complete their union, an action Schlup claimed was made impossible because of the broken limb.
Schlup said he had paid A$9,500 for Nelson in the expectation the bird would father up to 10 offspring a year for sale.
